To control for this, we define a \emph{controlled evaluation subset} that excludes any document where either model produces a truncated or repetitive output. An output is classified as \emph{truncated} if it reaches the generation length limit. An output is classified as \emph{repetitive} if it contains $\geq$3 consecutive identical triples or if the ratio of unique triples to total triples falls below 0.5 (when total $> 5$). The resulting subset contains 442 of 985 development documents (44.9\%). On this subset, the 1.7B evidence tax is +6.2pp (vs.\ +8.04pp on the full set), indicating that approximately 23\% of the raw gap is attributable to the no-evidence model's higher truncation rate. The positive direction is preserved, confirming that the 1.7B evidence benefit is genuine and not an artifact of output format differences.
